tldr: Aug 8 midday batch: OpenAI can no longer rule out the highest cybersecurity risk tier for its Astra model and paused parts of development, publishing its first frontier cyber evaluations — while the U.S. DOE launched the Genesis Open Models Initiative with Arcee. DeepSeek's V4 Flash 0731 posted ARC-AGI results, Anthropic makes Claude Code auto mode the default Aug 14, and an LLM designed 16 working viruses. Policy stacks up: EU AI Act enforcement went live Aug 2, Oracle banned AI-generated code from OpenJDK, and AWS sunset Bedrock Agents for AgentCore.

articles.title: OpenAI Flags Astra at Highest Cyber Risk, Pauses Parts of Development
articles.summary: Internal tests put Astra at the top of OpenAI's safety framework for the first time; parts of development paused after the Hugging Face breach.

articles.title: OpenAI Publishes First Frontier Cyber Evaluations for Astra
articles.summary: OpenAI shares preliminary cybersecurity evaluations for Astra and the steps it's taking to strengthen safeguards and security controls.

articles.title: U.S. DOE Launches Genesis Open Models Initiative with Arcee
articles.summary: The Department of Energy launches the Genesis Open Models Initiative, unveiling Genesis-Science-1, its first open-weight model for science.

articles.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 Posts Official ARC-AGI Results
articles.summary: ARC Prize publishes formal V4 Flash 0731 results — the day's top HN thread at 361 points with 222 comments debating open-model reasoning.

articles.title: Claude Cowork Expands to Web/Mobile; Code Auto Mode Default Aug 14
articles.summary: Cowork rolls out to web and mobile; Claude Code's auto mode becomes the default permission setting, replacing approval prompts.

articles.title: AI Designs 16 Working Viruses Never Seen in Nature
articles.summary: A language model built 16 functional viral genomes from scratch — the first functional genomes ever designed by an LLM, raising dual-use questions.

articles.title: Oracle Bans AI-Generated Code from OpenJDK
articles.summary: Oracle bars AI-written code from OpenJDK despite Ellison's claim it doesn't write its own — 337-point HN debate with 233 comments.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Regime Takes Effect Aug 2
articles.summary: GPAI enforcement powers, Article 50 transparency and the sanctioning framework apply from Aug 2; high-risk deadlines extended by the Digital Omnibus.

articles.title: AWS Closes Bedrock Agents Classic, Pushes AgentCore
articles.summary: Bedrock Agents is renamed 'Classic' and closed to new customers July 30; AWS steers new production agents to the AgentCore runtime.

articles.title: OpenAI Smart Speaker Expected 2027 at Over $300
articles.summary: OpenAI plans a screenless donut-shaped speaker with camera and mics for 2027, designed to learn from conversations — Altman's 'Her' device.

articles.title: Cloudflare Launches Kitesurf, a Browser for AI Agents
articles.summary: A cloud-hosted browser optimized for context windows and token costs instead of visual chrome — infra rebuilt for the agent era.

articles.title: Hugging Face Diffusers Flaws Allow Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-44827)
articles.summary: Three TOCTOU flaws (CVSS 8.8) bypass trust_remote_code so crafted model repos execute code during pipeline loading; patched in 0.38.0.

articles.title: Natural Raises $30M as 'Stripe for AI Agents'
articles.summary: Payment startup Natural closes a $30M Series A ($40M total) to build transaction rails purpose-built for AI-agent payments.

articles.title: Databricks Cuts AI Coding Spend 70% at Scale
articles.summary: Databricks details how it drove AI coding costs down 70% — 132-point HN thread on managing agent code spend at enterprise scale.

articles.title: Suno Tightens Rules on Spam and Copyright Concerns
articles.summary: Suno adds guidelines and download limits after AI music was used to game streaming platforms; faces German copyright ruling pressure.

articles.title: Wan-Animate-2: End-to-End Character Animation from Driving Videos
articles.summary: Alibaba's new Diffusion Transformer framework consumes driving videos directly, dropping intermediate motion extractors for better identity preservation.
